newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet MD bitter after Italy vote setback.
newsitem.headline: Stet MD bitter after Italy vote setback.

text.p: The managing director of Stet said he was bitter about a parliamentary vote against transfer of the telecom holding to the Treasury, adding that Italians did not understand the importance of the state sell-off programme.
The lower house of parliament dealt the government a sharp blow late on Wednesday when it voted down a proposal to transfer control of Stet from state holding IRI to the Treasury.
"There is bitterness for this vote which was so unexpected," Stet's Ernesto Pascale told La Repubblica newspaper.
"For us it doesn't matter if IRI or the Treasury owns us. What does matter is to see that there are still doubts over the privatisations," he added.
Stet was slated for sell-off in 1996, but the privatisation has been postponed to this year after parliament failed to get the necessary legislation in place.
"One has the feeling that this country still hasn't understood the importance of the sell-offs," Pascale said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition lost Wednesday's vote after its ally, the hardleft Communist Refoundation, abstained. The Refoundation secures the government's majority in the lower house and is ideologically opposed to the Stet sale.
Pascale said the Milan bourse was ready to absorb the Stet privatisation and added that he hoped the company's share price would not suffer as a result of the unexpected defeat.

The Treasury late on Wednesday sought to play down the parliamentary set-back, saying the vote would not sink the transfer plan because it was attached to part of the 1997 budget and effectively had "already taken place."
